title: Upgrade to support OpenMRS Platform 3.0
body:
Updates addresshierarchy so it builds against, and runs on, openmrs-core master (Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT: Java 21, Jakarta EE, Spring 7, Hibernate 7). Same approach as the platform 3 upgrades of calculation (openmrs/openmrs-module-calculation#19), legacyui and webservices.rest.

## Changes
- Versions and build:
  - Module version is now 4.0.0-SNAPSHOT, on Platform 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT (with `openmrs-bom` imported) and legacyui 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT.
  - Builds with Java 21 and `-parameters`, with surefire 3.5.4.
  - The PowerMock exclusions and `javax.servlet-api` are removed.
  - The api module no longer depends on openmrs-web.
  - commons-codec is no longer declared, so it comes from core.
- `config.xml` now sets `require_version` to 3.0.0. CI (release workflow and Bamboo) uses JDK 21.
- DAO:
  - All Hibernate Criteria queries are now HQL, with the same case-insensitive and "contains" semantics.
  - `load` becomes `getReference`, `saveOrUpdate`/`update` become `HibernateUtil.saveOrUpdate`, and `delete`/`save` become `remove`/`persist`.
  - `createSQLQuery` becomes `createNativeQuery`, with 1-based positional parameters.
- hbm id generators change from `native` to `identity`.
- `AddressField` was mapped with `org.hibernate.type.EnumType`, which Hibernate 7 removed. It now uses core's `org.openmrs.api.db.hibernate.type.StringEnumType` (`enumClass` parameter), and the stored value (the enum name) is unchanged.
- commons-lang becomes lang3, and `javax.servlet` becomes `jakarta.servlet`.
- Tests:
  - Migrated to JUnit 5.
  - The test context uses JobRunr's `InMemoryStorageProvider`, so contexts restarted after `deleteAllData()` don't fail on `JOBRUNR_MIGRATIONS`.
- **The exti18n integration tests are excluded for now.** exti18n 1.x itself can't run on Platform 3.0 (its interceptors extend the removed `EmptyInterceptor`). It stays a compile-only dependency, kept off the test classpath. Re-enable those tests once exti18n is ported.

## Depends on
- openmrs/openmrs-core#6633, so that core's `StringEnumType` can load `AddressField` through the module classloader. Without it the session factory fails to start with "Enum class not found".

## Verification
- Built and tested against core master with #6633: `mvn clean install` passes, with api 66 tests (2 already `@Ignore`d) and omod 12.
- With all 31 O3 reference application modules upgraded to Platform 3, on openmrs-core master plus the core fixes openmrs/openmrs-core#6629, #6631, #6633, #6635, #6637 and #6639 (`mvn jetty:run`, MySQL 8): every module starts, logging in through the UI works, and core message codes resolve.
  - The session factory, which resolves `AddressField` through `StringEnumType`, starts, and `/module/addresshierarchy/admin/manageAddressHierarchy.form` renders.

title: ADDR-148: Improve batch-loading performance
body:
<!--- Add a pull request title above in this format -->
<!--- real example: 'ADDR-128 Add foreignKeyTableName to liquibase constraints' -->
<!--- 'ADDR-JiraIssueNumber JiraIssueTitle' -->
## Description of what I changed
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
<!--- It can simply be your commit message, which you must have -->

It's been reported that the Address Hierarchy module is very slow with a very large hierarchy set. Using an example hierarchy of 120k-ish rows takes about 15 minutes on my machine. With this change, it takes about 45 seconds. The story is even better if only a few rows change as previously that would recursively load parents one at a time and now this is done in a single query.

Note that to get to these results and to factor out a quadratic growth in the number of database queries, the bulk loading here is done through raw SQL, which should be safe enough at initialization. Much of the overhead this removes was simply caused by Hibernate trying to keep all in-memory entities current across a given transaction.

As a result of this speed-up, loading or updating the address hierarchy is now done in a single transaction so it's an all-or-nothing thing.

title: ADDR-147: Return no children when every mapped address level has a value
body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Ian Bacher** · [Slack thread](https://openmrs.slack.com/archives/C02UNMKFH8V/p1789733140211449?thread_ts=1789733140.211449&cid=C02UNMKFH8V)_

see https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/ADDR-147

## Description of what I changed

**Before.** The ajax handler `getChildAddressHierarchyEntries` takes a pipe-separated `searchString` such as `UNITED STATES|MASSACHUSETTS|PLYMOUTH COUNTY`, walks the mapped address hierarchy levels assigning one token per level, and then returns the possible values for the *next* level down via `levels.get(i)`. When the caller had already supplied a value for every mapped level, `i` was equal to `levels.size()` and that final lookup threw `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. The in-loop guard was meant to catch exactly this, but it tested `levels.size() <= i - 1`, which only trips one index *past* the `levels.get(i)` it was protecting, so it never fired in time.

Because these `.form` handlers have no exception-to-status mapping, the exception did not surface as a 5xx: it reached callers as HTTP 200 with a serialized stack trace in the response body. A client that parsed that body as JSON simply broke, which is how this showed up as a failure in the O3 registration form.

**After.** When a value has been supplied for every mapped level there is no level below the last one, so there are no child entries to list and the handler returns an empty JSON array (`[]`) — the same response it already gives for a level that legitimately has no children. No new status code and no new exception type, since other callers depend on this endpoint's current contract.

## How

Two lines in `AddressHierarchyAjaxController.getChildAddressHierarchyEntries`:

- the in-loop guard now tests the index actually about to be dereferenced (`levels.size() <= i`), so it protects the `levels.get(i)` on the following line and still raises `AddressHierarchyModuleException` when more values are supplied than there are mapped levels (including the "no mapped levels at all" case the message already describes);
- the post-loop lookup is only performed while `i` is in range, so `levels.get(i)` is now unreachable with an out-of-range index and `childEntryNames` stays the empty list it was initialised to.

Tests added to `AddressHierarchyAjaxControllerTest` (the existing omod dataset has five mapped levels: country, state, county, city, neighborhood):

- one token per mapped level returns `[]` instead of throwing — the ADDR-147 case;
- four tokens still return the neighborhoods below the named city, so the in-range path is unchanged;
- more tokens than mapped levels still fails fast with `AddressHierarchyModuleException`.

The other five handlers in this controller are untouched, and nothing here touches `produces` or content negotiation. ADDR-145 / #66 (the service-level empty-hierarchy fix) and the O3-side guard are separate changes; this PR only touches the controller, so it should not overlap with #66.

- [x] I have **added tests** to cover my changes.

CI is the first real check, which is why this is opened as a draft.

title: ADDR-145: Fix NPE and poisoned empty address cache when no address hierarchy is configured
body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Ian Bacher, Pius Rubangakene** · [Slack thread](https://openmrs.slack.com/archives/C02UNMKFH8V/p1789733140211449?thread_ts=1789733140.211449&cid=C02UNMKFH8V)_

see https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/ADDR-145

### Before

On a server where no address hierarchy levels are configured, the very first address search blew up. `getTopAddressHierarchyLevel()` returns `null` when no level has a null parent (i.e. no levels at all), and `getAddressHierarchyEntriesByLevel(null)` returned `null` rather than an empty list, so the `for` loop that walks the top-level entries while building the full address cache threw a `NullPointerException`.

The more damaging half is what happened next. `getAddressesForLocale()` put the freshly created (still empty) map into `fullAddressCache` *before* running that loop, so the NPE left a published, permanently empty cache behind. Every later search then found a map for the locale, skipped the build entirely, and returned an empty address list as a perfectly successful response — no error, no retry, nothing that would ever rebuild it. That matches the reported symptom of a first request failing and subsequent requests quietly returning nothing useful.

### After

An unconfigured hierarchy yields an empty result on the first call and on every call after it, with no exception and no stuck cache. Once levels and entries are configured (an entry save resets the cache), the cache builds normally. A build that throws or is abandoned part-way through no longer leaves anything behind that a later caller could mistake for a completed cache.

### How

- `AddressHierarchyServiceImpl.getAddressHierarchyEntriesByLevel(level)` returns `Collections.emptyList()` instead of `null` for a null level. Every caller in `api/` and `omod/` was audited: none treats `null` as distinct from empty — the two that check at all (`ManageAddressHierarchyController.getSampleEntries()` and `AddressLayoutPortletController`) use `entries != null && entries.size() > 0`, which behaves identically, and the remaining call sites iterate or `addAll()` the result and would have NPE'd on `null` anyway. The interface javadoc now states the contract.
- `getAddressesForLocale()` wraps the build in `try`/`finally` and removes the locale's map from `fullAddressCache` unless the build ran to completion. The map still has to be published up front, because `initializeFullAddressCacheHelper()` writes into the cached map and uses its absence to detect a concurrent reset (ADDR-144), so removing it on failure is the way to guarantee a partial or failed build is never served as a success — an exception mid-loop is covered as well as the abandoned-build path.
- Regression tests: `AddressHierarchyServiceUnconfiguredTest` runs against a database that never had `addressHierarchy-dataset.xml` loaded and asserts that `searchAddresses()` returns empty on the first *and* second call without throwing; plus a test in `AddressHierarchyServiceTest` that the accessor returns an empty list for a null level.

### Notes

- **Introduced by ADDR-126** (`108d84d`, first released in **2.15.2**), which lifted the cache-building loop out of `initializeFullAddressCache()` — where it sat behind an `getAddressHierarchyEntryCount() > 0` guard — into the new `getAddressesForLocale()`, which has no such guard and is called directly from `searchAddresses()`.
- **Distinct from ADDR-144** (#65). That one was a race between a build and a concurrent `resetFullAddressCache()`; this one needs no concurrency at all, just an unconfigured hierarchy.
- **The earlier `produces = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE` approach has been dropped at the maintainer's request** — @ibacher wants content negotiation on these endpoints to keep working, and would rather see a proper REST resource than these ajax `.form` handlers pinned to JSON. That commit has been removed from this branch and replaced with the fix above.
- **Why the unconfigured-hierarchy test gets it

title: ADDR-144: Fix NPE on full-address-cache build race, speed up CSV import
body:
## Summary

Loading a large address hierarchy CSV (~32,000 entries, via `AddressConfigurationLoader`) on a fresh install can take a very long time, and partway through, the full-address-cache build throws a `NullPointerException`:

```
ERROR - AbstractAddressHierarchyTask.run(34) | An error occurred while running scheduled address hierarchy task
java.lang.NullPointerException: null
    at ...AddressHierarchyServiceImpl.initializeFullAddressCacheHelper(AddressHierarchyServiceImpl.java:766)
    ... (repeated recursive frames)
    at ...AddressHierarchyServiceImpl.getAddressesForLocale(AddressHierarchyServiceImpl.java:736)
    at ...AddressHierarchyServiceImpl.initializeFullAddressCache(AddressHierarchyServiceImpl.java:716)
    at ...scheduler.InitializeFullAddressCacheTask.execute(InitializeFullAddressCacheTask.java:16)
```

Not fatal (it's a background task that logs and stops), but it means the full-address cache never gets built that run, and it points at a real bug plus a real performance problem, both fixed here.

## Fix 1: race condition between cache build and cache reset (the NPE)

`initializeFullAddressCache()` / `getAddressesForLocale()` are `synchronized` and together recursively walk the whole hierarchy tree to build `fullAddressCache`. `resetFullAddressCache()` - called after every `saveAddressHierarchyEntry()`/`saveAddressHierarchyEntries()` - is **not** synchronized:

```java
public void resetFullAddressCache() {
    this.fullAddressCache = null;
    this.fullAddressCacheInitialized = false;
}
```

If a build is triggered on one thread (e.g. `AddressHierarchyActivator.contextRefreshed()`) while another thread is still saving entries (e.g. `AddressHierarchyActivator.started()` -> `AddressConfigurationLoader`, which can take minutes for a large CSV), the unsynchronized reset can null `fullAddressCache` mid-recursion, and the next read throws.

Fix: `initializeFullAddressCacheHelper` now returns a boolean, and both the recursion and the top-level loop in `getAddressesForLocale` abort as soon as it comes back `false`, instead of continuing to walk the rest of the tree against a cache that no longer exists. Any subsequent entry save already flips `fullAddressCacheInitialized` back to `false`, so a later call to `initializeFullAddressCache()` rebuilds correctly once entries have stopped changing - no data is lost. Note this narrows the race between a build and a concurrent reset, it doesn't close it: `resetFullAddressCache()` is intentionally left unsynchronized (it's called after every CSV import batch and must never block on a concurrent full-cache build), so `fullAddressCache` can still be nulled between the check and its use a little further down in the same synchronized methods - just a much smaller window than the one this fixes.

Added a regression test (`initializeFullAddressCache_shouldNotThrowIfCacheIsResetDuringBuild`) that resets the cache and then directly invokes the private recursive helper on both a leaf and a non-leaf entry, asserting it returns `false` in both cases instead of throwing or silently continuing to walk the tree.

## Fix 2: CSV import batch size is far too small for large hierarchies

`AddressHierarchyImportUtil.ENTRY_BATCH_SIZE` was `10` - each batch is its own committed transaction. For ~32,000 entries that's ~3,200 separate transactions/commits. Raised to `500`, cutting transaction count by roughly 50x with minimal added per-batch memory pressure.

Benchmarked end-to-end against the actual ~32,363-entry PIH Malawi CSV: in-memory H2 dropped from ~2.8-3.7s to ~1.8-2.0s (~1.6x), and MySQL 5.6 (Docker, loopback, `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=1` - full commit durability, not relaxed) dropped from ~4.9-5.2s to ~4.0-4.1s (~1.2-1.3x). Real, but modest - most of the actual ~20 minute production load time is likely coming from somewhere else (real network latency to the DB, disk I/O, or the O(n) child-entry lookups during import/cache-build), not batch commit count alone. title: Separate OWASP dependency check into its own job
body:
## Summary
- Separate OWASP dependency check into a standalone workflow job
- OWASP check only runs on push and workflow_dispatch (not on PRs)
- Build job no longer runs the OWASP check inline or needs the NVD_API_KEY secret

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify build job still passes
- [ ] Verify OWASP dependency check runs on push to the default branch
- [ ] Verify OWASP dependency check does not run on pull requests
